long_biography.plain_text:
The first policies Ely Kaplansky sold for his Brookline insurance agency came from a rented room, after he had learned the trade as a teenage registration runner. Insurers would not appoint his new firm directly, so he began as a designated broker for motor cover. He spent a decade building the business before securing a standard agency contract.

Kaplansky bought established agencies as their owners retired, using their existing books of business to extend his reach across Massachusetts. He argued that independent agents should explain coverage rather than compete only on the lowest premium. He also chaired the Massachusetts Association of Insurance Agents, bringing an agency builder’s perspective to the profession’s leadership.
